## Beware the Frankenfloor


**October 26, 2026**


[back to posts](https://www.bc.com/blog/)


Not every floor system is created as a whole.


Some become Frankenfloors – assembled piece by piece with joists or other components from different manufacturers used in the same application. Each product may be well suited for the job, but coordinating different product information, design assumptions, tolerances, and installation requirements can add frightening complexity to a project.


### **A Smarter Way to Frame**


Boise Cascade engineered wood products are designed to work together to create quiet, solid floors, keeping scary, creaky floors to haunted houses.


When joists, beams, rim board, and their related components are specified and designed in tandem, project teams can work from a more consistent set of requirements and expectations.


That coordinated approach can help simplify:


- Product selection and specification


- Determining load and span limits


- Ease of installation


- Communication among project teams


- Warranty coverage


- Access to technical resources and engineering support


With product sizing and performance characteristics designed to work together, teams can spend less time sorting through information from multiple sources and more time moving projects forward.


### **Support Made Simple**


A floor is more than the sum of its individual parts.


Many elements work together and contribute to how the finished floor performs and feels underfoot. A system-based approach considers those interactions from the beginning.


Boise Cascade brings together reliable engineered wood products, software solutions, technical resources, and expert engineering support to help project teams make informed decisions throughout the life of a project. Our Value Added Solutions software can help specifiers and designers evaluate floor layouts, select appropriate products, and coordinate framing details more efficiently. By bringing product information and design considerations together in one workflow, these tools can help make it easier to move from concept to construction-ready plans.


The result is a connected set of solutions designed to help project teams work with greater clarity, efficiency, and confidence.


### **Floors That Don’t Come Back to Haunt You**


Homeowners may not know the name of every component beneath their floors, but they often notice when they feel noisy or uneven.


Building a Frankenfloor does not automatically mean it will perform poorly. However, coordinating multiple product systems can require additional time and effort – both valuable resources on the jobsite.


For designers and builders alike, a coordinated system can mean fewer details to reconcile, more consistent information from design through installation, and easier communication across the project team. It can also help address questions earlier, avoid preventable issues and callbacks, and protect the reputation they’ve worked hard to build.


By supporting a smoother process from specification through installation, a Boise Cascade EWP floor system can help build with confidence and leave the creaking floors to the haunted houses.


### **Wishing you a safe and happy Halloween!**
